title: Analog Bits Targets the Power Challenge at the Heart of Next-Generation Chips - Semiwiki
gist: Analog Bits is putting power-delivery and on-die sensing IP into a customer test-chip tapeout on TSMC's A14 process while demonstrating N2P real-time power observability with Cerebras, Arm and Socionext at TSMC's 2026 OIP forum — positioning pinless PVT sensors, on-die LDOs with droop detection and microwatt PLLs as the answer to power becoming the binding constraint on AI silicon.

insights.claim: Power has become a fundamental constraint on computing progress, with AI infrastructure operating at megawatt scale while individual SoCs inside it can consume several kilowatts each.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Kilowatt-class single SoCs reset thermal, packaging and power-delivery requirements across the whole data-center BOM.
insights.quote: AI infrastructure may operate at the megawatt scale, while the individual SoCs powering it can consume several kilowatts.

insights.claim: Transistor performance keeps increasing without a proportional reduction in operating voltage, producing greater power density, more heat and tighter limits on how much performance can safely be extracted from advanced silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The end of voltage scaling is the root cause behind demand for power-management IP — a structural, not cyclical, driver.
insights.locator: At the same time, transistor performance continues

insights.claim: Real-time on-die observability lets designers monitor conditions close to individual cores and functional blocks instead of relying only on board- or package-level measurements, enabling localized voltage and frequency response rather than system-wide control.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Granularity of measurement is the new axis of competition in power management IP.

insights.claim: Localized power control can improve energy efficiency while reducing the risk of voltage droops, timing failures, overheating and premature device degradation, making it a reliability play as well as an efficiency play.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reliability framing widens the buyer set to automotive and long-life data-center parts, not just efficiency-driven AI chips.
insights.locator: Such localized control can improve energy efficiency

insights.claim: Analog Bits' remote pinless PVT sensors deliver untrimmed temperature accuracy of plus or minus 3.5 degrees Celsius and its PLLs operate at microwatt-class power levels.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Specific specs that competing IP vendors must beat; untrimmed accuracy matters because trimming adds test cost.
insights.locator: At N2P, the company will demonstrate

insights.claim: At N2P the company demonstrates integrated on-die low-dropout regulators with glitch-catching and voltage-droop detection alongside pinless PVT sensors and low-power PLLs, combining sensing with the regulation needed to act on it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sense-plus-actuate bundling is harder to displace than point IP and supports higher royalty capture per chip.
insights.locator: At N2P, the company will demonstrate

insights.claim: Conventional analog functions require dedicated supply pins and supporting circuitry that complicate packages and board designs, so eliminating those requirements reduces cost, simplifies integration and makes the same IP easier to scale across large SoCs and chiplet architectures.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pin-count reduction compounds in chiplet designs where the same sensor block is instantiated many times — the real scaling argument.
insights.locator: The pinless design approach is also significant

insights.claim: A Socionext paper on pinless PLL and PVT-sensor IP for data-center and automotive SoCs explicitly emphasizes eliminating dedicated analog power supplies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Third-party validation from a design-services house signals the pinless approach is being adopted, not just marketed.

insights.claim: Analog Bits' IP will be included in an upcoming customer test-chip tapeout using TSMC's A14 process, intended to make its next-generation IP silicon-proven and reduce integration risk for early adopters of the node.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: IP readiness on A14 is a leading indicator of which node the customer base is actually committing to for 2028 products.
insights.locator: The company announced that its IP will be included

insights.claim: Customers generally require proof that critical IP works in actual silicon before committing it to expensive products, which is why test-chip participation rather than datasheet capability is the meaningful milestone for an IP vendor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A diligence rule for IP companies: count silicon-proven instances, not announced products.
insights.quote: Customers generally want proof that critical IP works in actual silicon before committing it to expensive products.

insights.claim: Analog Bits says billions of its IP cores have already been fabricated across processes ranging from 0.35 micron down to 2 nanometers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A 30-year node span is the incumbency argument; it also means legacy-node royalties cushion leading-edge timing risk.
insights.locator: Analog Bits says billions of its IP cores

insights.claim: Analog Bits is co-presenting with Cerebras on on-die power management for scalable SoCs and chiplet architectures and with Arm on integrated power and clock management for core-level optimization in N3P and N2P data-center processors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Named partners at the top of the AI-silicon stack are the strongest available evidence of design-win traction.
insights.locator: Analog Bits will outline the broader technical case
